# Frozen optical/tone stage diagnosis

## Scope and status

This diagnostic is prepared but **not compiled or executed**. Production sources,
the baseline JAR, and candidate JAR remain unchanged. Root owns the serialized
compile and measurement schedule under `cr3-performance.lock`.

The completed packaged comparison has 456 exact, fitting imports, as reported
by root. The observed Java 21 wide-capture regression is material in both
collectors: Serial aggregate CPU 2180 to 2510 ms (three forks), and G1 2165 to
2665 ms (two forks). Serial baseline per-fork CPU medians are 3060, 2180, 2150 ms
versus candidate 2510, 2660, 2250 ms; the reported median-of-medians changes are
-15.1% CPU benefit and -7.45% elapsed benefit. Java 25 improves across the Serial
cells and in G1 for G5 and wide, while G1 EOS is approximately neutral. The
portable fusion candidate is not accepted as-is. These results establish the
performance problem but do not identify the cause.

This is an investigation of that discrepancy, not a proposed production fix or
an additional performance acceptance benchmark. Complete imports remain the
acceptance measure.

## Existing reusable probe

The original source is `/workspace/scratch/80a209e8f5df/OpticalStagesProbe.java`.
An identical repository copy is at
`Photographer/docs/cr3/camera-rendering-performance-2026-11-25/OpticalStagesProbe.java`.
There is another scratch copy under `perf-final/OpticalStagesProbe.java`.

That probe decodes neutral RGB16 once and resets a reusable image before timing
optics and tone independently. It always calls sequential public optics and
tone, so running it against the candidate cannot measure its fused operation.
It also hashes the optical image between stages on the last iteration only,
which changes the last tone invocation's cache state. The new probe avoids an
inter-stage hash in combined/sequential measurements.

## Hypotheses to distinguish

1. **A changed tone loop or its invocation context contributes to the regression.**
   Compare public `tone` on the same optically corrected template across frozen
   JARs. If the difference repeats, the optional scalar kernel cases can narrow
   it to the existing three-array versus four-array loop and split blue input.
   A source-level signature difference is not proof of a generated-code effect.
2. **The fused optical/tone data flow changes warmed combined-stage cost.**
   Compare `combined` across JARs and compare `combined` against `sequential`
   within the candidate, using fresh JVMs and counterbalanced fork order.
   Candidate `sequential` retains the modified tone kernel, but restores the
   public sequential composition without changing production code.
3. **The observed variation is outside these stages or is sensitive to JVM/host state.**
   Preserve every iteration, including warmup, and record process CPU, elapsed
   time, collection counts/time, and aggregate compilation time. Similar stage
   results alongside an unstable complete-import difference would narrow the
   investigation; it would not by itself prove that host noise caused it.

## Driver behavior

`OpticalToneStageDiagnostic.java` compiles against either frozen JAR using Java
21 APIs. It accepts only the two known JAR SHA-256 identities and records the
actual JAR path/hash, input file/hash, Java version/arguments, dimensions,
requested workers, and every full-image hash. No library class is copied,
recompiled, replaced, or instrumented.

The input is decoded once to full RGB16 with both optics and tone disabled.
This neutral image's hash must match across JARs. Tone-only modes apply optics
once outside timing and retain the resulting fixed corrected template. Each
iteration resets the same independently allocated dense working image from that
template before starting the timer. Split-blue setup is also outside the timer.
Only the selected production operation is timed. Every warmup and measured output
is hashed in full afterwards and checked against an untimed sequential oracle.
The template is checked again at the end for unintended mutation.

The oracle initializes shared tables before any timed iteration. This probe
therefore diagnoses warmed stage behavior; it must not be used for first-import
or lazy-initialization performance claims.

| Mode | Timed operation | Comparison |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `combined` | Baseline: optics then tone. Candidate: existing fused public operation. | Principal stage comparison across JARs. |
| `sequential` | Public optics then public tone on either JAR. | Candidate control that retains its changed kernel but omits fusion. |
| `optical` | Public optics only. | Optional check of unchanged optical math under its changed wrapper. |
| `tone` | Public tone only, on fixed optically corrected samples. | Isolates the normal tone path and its actual worker partitioning. |
| `kernel-alias` | Existing private/package kernel directly, one thread and aliased blue input/output. | Baseline three-array versus candidate four-array kernel; excludes worker scheduling. |
| `kernel-split` | Candidate's existing four-array kernel with separately reset blue input. | Candidate-only check of the non-aliased blue data flow. Baseline rejects this mode. |

The candidate combined method and scalar kernels use one reflective invocation
per whole image, with method lookup and argument-array construction outside the
timer. This adds a small invocation cost and can change JIT call context; kernel
results are diagnostic only. The public `tone` path is the stronger evidence
for the actual worker context. All arguments are original values; no alternate
arithmetic or copied tone implementation is introduced.

`process_cpu_ms` includes all JVM threads, such as compiler and collector work.
`caller_cpu_ms` is useful for the single-thread kernel modes, but excludes worker
CPU in public parallel modes. GC and compilation counters are coarse diagnostic
counters, not a profiler or a causal attribution. `kernel_workers` is 1 for
kernel modes and -1 for public modes whose production scheduler chooses stripes.

## Bounded execution plan for root

Do not run alongside current imports. After the existing serialized sequence,
compile this one driver with Java 25 `javac --release 21`, using only the baseline
JAR and a separate `stage-diagnosis/classes` output directory. Run the resulting
identical driver class against one frozen JAR at a time. Keep the full-import
heap, CPU affinity, worker setting, collector, and Java executable unchanged.

Start with Java 21, `sample-wide.cr3`, two counterbalanced fresh forks, five
warmups and seven measured iterations:

- Baseline `combined`, candidate `combined`, and candidate `sequential`.
- Baseline `tone` and candidate `tone`.

One fork should put baseline before candidate; the other should reverse that
order. Use separate fresh JVMs for each case, retain all raw JSON lines/stderr,
and stop expanding if those cases already resolve the decision. If tone-only
repeats a difference, use baseline and candidate `kernel-alias`, then candidate
`kernel-split`. Add `optical` or another runtime/capture only to resolve a specific
remaining question.

Example compile command (for root to run under the existing lock):

```bash
/workspace/scratch/743c18c2db2f/math-reach.4xbJwv/jdk25/bin/javac --release 21 -cp /workspace/scratch/80a209e8f5df/cr3-pipeline-throughput/baseline/benchmarks.jar -d /workspace/scratch/80a209e8f5df/cr3-pipeline-throughput/stage-diagnosis/classes /workspace/scratch/80a209e8f5df/cr3-pipeline-throughput/stage-diagnosis/OpticalToneStageDiagnostic.java
```

Example single case (for root to run under the existing lock, redirecting to a
new result file rather than overwriting observations):

```bash
taskset -c 4-7 /usr/lib/jvm/java-21-openjdk-amd64/bin/java -Xmx768m -XX:+UseSerialGC -XX:ActiveProcessorCount=4 -Djava.awt.headless=true -cp /workspace/scratch/80a209e8f5df/cr3-pipeline-throughput/stage-diagnosis/classes:/workspace/scratch/80a209e8f5df/cr3-pipeline-throughput/candidate/benchmarks.jar OpticalToneStageDiagnostic combined /workspace/scratch/80a209e8f5df/Photographer/canon-cr3-imageio/src/test/resources/samples/sample-wide.cr3 5 7 4
```

Before interpreting timing, require identical `input_sha256`, `neutral_sha256`,
dimensions, JVM settings and appropriate `stage_input_sha256` across the paired
cases. The combined/sequential final hashes must match each other. Tone and
kernel modes must match the combined final hash, because their corrected input
was prepared with the same optics. The optical-only hash must match the tone
modes' stage-input hash. Preserve warmup and per-fork results; do not discard
slower forks or choose a different warmup count after inspecting a favored arm.

No execution or causal conclusion is recorded at preparation time.
